summary: On April 18, 2024, at approximately 1422 hours, Officer P. Sullivan responded to a grand theft at Bay Area Electronics, 3200 Lakeshore Avenue, Oakland, CA. Two suspects executed a coordinated retail theft using a distraction technique. A white female (approximately 25-30, blonde hair, green army jacket) engaged sales associate Kevin Marsh in conversation about headphones while a white male (approximately 30, shaved head, goatee, gray sweatshirt) accessed the high-value electronics display at the rear of the store using a magnet key suspected to have been stolen during a prior visit. The male suspect removed three Apple iPhone 15 Pro Max units ($1,199 each) and two Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra units ($1,299 each), placing them in a lined bag designed to defeat EAS tags. Both suspects exited through the rear emergency door onto Rand Avenue at approximately 1412 hours and departed in a silver SUV (possibly Toyota RAV4, partial California plate beginning with 7M) northbound on Rand Avenue. Total estimated loss: $6,195. Store manager Henry Yamamoto noted this is the second major theft in 30 days (see Case #2024-00298) with a similar MO, suggesting an organized retail theft operation. The case has been referred to the Organized Retail Crime Task Force and assigned to Detective A. Morales.
